summary.text: Chloe Bond is standing for the Animal Justice Party in Eildon at the 2026 Victorian election. A lawyer based in Wesburn, she works at a community legal centre, mainly on cases involving victims of crime and family violence, after earlier work in private practice and at Victoria Legal Aid. This is her fourth campaign for the party: she ran in Eildon in 2022, for the Yarra Ranges council in 2024 and in the federal seat of Casey in 2025.

previous_candidacies.note: The ward is named in the title of a Star Mail report cited by Wikipedia's 2024 local elections article; Wikipedia's Yarra Ranges Shire article shows the ward held by another councillor since 2012.

priorities.text: A shift away from animal agriculture towards farming without animals
An end to native forest logging and to recreational duck shooting
Harsher penalties for animal cruelty and legal recognition of animals as sentient
Opposes the horse racing and greyhound racing industries

summary.text: Cindy McLeish is a Liberal member of the Legislative Assembly, elected for Seymour in 2010 and holding Eildon since 2014. She was deputy leader of the Victorian Liberals from 2018 to 2021 and is shadow minister for women, family violence prevention, and WorkSafe and the TAC. She is recontesting Eildon in 2026.

occupation.text: Management consultant; earlier a secondary teacher

prior_roles.role: Shadow Minister for WorkSafe and TAC
Shadow Minister for Women; Prevention of Family Violence

Shadow Minister for Environment and Climate Change
Deputy Leader of the Liberal Party
Shadow Minister for Tourism, Major Events and Sport

priorities.text: Investment in job-creating industries such as farming, tourism and hospitality
Country access to health, mental health services and roads on par with the city

Support for veterans and serving defence personnel

summary.text: Dylan Little is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Eildon at the 2026 Victorian election. He is an arborist, a member of the Australian Workers' Union, and grew up in Wesburn. He describes years of activism on issues including racism, public housing and refugees, and more recently on Palestine.

priorities.text: I believe in a society that's more sustainable, more equitable, and just
State action on the housing shortage and the cost of living
Standing up to corporate and wealthy interests in Parliament

sources.title: Eildon: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Dylan Little, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Joshua Mosely is the Family First candidate for Eildon at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. His party page says he lives in Euroa, leads Euroa Christian Fellowship as pastor, works as a school chaplain and has 25 years in ministry, and has also worked in aircraft maintenance, earthmoving, truck and bus driving and outdoor education while running a small business. A Family First candidate of the same name stood for Williamstown at the 2022 state election.

prior_roles.role: Small business owner (practical and maintenance services)

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia lists a Joshua Mosely as the Family First candidate; no source says he is the 2026 Eildon candidate, though the name and party match.

priorities.text: Directing regional investment to local infrastructure, services and projects
Supporting families and people who are vulnerable
Recognising what regional communities contribute to the state

summary.text: Kevin Gibson is Labor's candidate for Eildon at the 2026 Victorian election. A mechanical engineer by training, he spent about 25 years in automotive and manufacturing businesses and later managed Pallotti College in Millgrove, where he lives. He now drives a school bus and is a volunteer firefighter with the Wesburn-Millgrove CFA brigade.

prior_roles.role: Engineer and executive, automotive and manufacturing industry

priorities.text: Health and support services that local families can reach
Better schools, services and infrastructure for the Eildon area
Backing local businesses

sources.title: Eildon: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Kevin Gibson, Candidate for Eildon, Victorian Labor

summary.text: Talia Gulpilil is the Greens candidate for Eildon at the 2026 Victorian election. She works as a First Nations organiser and heads a firm offering strategic policy and advisory services. She was raised in Healesville and still lives there with her family.

priorities.text: everyone deserves a safe, secure and affordable place to call home
Greater public spending on public housing and on homes people can genuinely afford
Better protections for renters, and tackling what drives homelessness

summary.text: Tom Ward is an independent candidate for Eildon at the 2026 Victorian election, with the backing of a local community group called Eildon Unheard. The ABC's guide says he has worked behind a bar and once operated a gourmet mushroom business in the district. His campaign website, Eildon Forward, carried no biography as at early November 2026.
